headline: Votes on a $1.5 million Fire supplemental appropriation and a $1.1 million Free Cash transfer for LPD, plus an executive session on a tax increment exemption agreement.
summary: The agenda includes budget votes, including $1.5 million for Fire and $1.1 million for LPD. It also includes an executive session on a Tax Increment Exemption agreement with 78-80 Middlesex Street, LLC.
items: Proclamation - Breast Cancer Awareness
Citation - Kolthyda (Nina) Hok
Motion: Identify underutilized public spaces and explore improvements to increase foot traffic downtown
Motion: Information on the anticipated opening of Bicentennial Park on Jackson Street
Motion: Examine the on-ramp from Centralville to the Hunts Falls Rotary, including yield signage
Motion: Public Flock camera demonstration with a question-and-answer session
Motion: Send a letter opposing repurposing the ICC into any type of shelter
Motion: Report on the yearly cost of a property tax increase freeze for seniors over 75 who have owned and lived in their home more than 30 years

CITY COUNCIL - MOTIONS
C. McDonough - Req. City Mgr. Have The Appropriate Departments Work With 
Community Partners Such As The LDNA, Small Businesses, Event Organizers, And 
Others To Identify Underutilized Public Spaces And Explore Potential Improvements 
To Increase Foot Traffic In And Around The Downtown. 
C. McDonough - Req. City Mgr. Provide Information Regarding The Anticipated 
Opening Of The Bicentennial Park On Jackson Street. 
C. Robinson - Req. City Mgr. Have The Proper Department Examine And Address 
Through Proper Channels The On-Ramp Leading To The Hunts Falls Rotary From 
Centralville, Including Yield Signage.
C. Robinson / C. Descoteaux - Req. City Mgr. Have The Proper Departments Work 
Together To Offer A Public Flock Camera Demonstration With A Question-And-
Answer Session.
C. Robinson / M. Gitschier - Req. City Mgr. And The Council Send A Letter Clearly 
Stating Opposition To Repurposing The ICC Into Any Type Of Shelter Due To The 
City’s Economic And Developmental Goals And Objectives.
M. Gitschier - Req. City Mgr. Provide The City Council With A Report On The Yearly 
Cost Of Providing A Freeze On Property Tax Increases For Any Senior Citizen Over 
The Age Of 75 Who Have Lived In And Owned Their Current Residence For More 
Than 30 Years.
